program.name: Residential Assistance for Families in Transition (RAFT)
program.provider: Commonwealth of Massachusetts; application help from Way Finders
program.description: The Commonwealth's RAFT program helps households stay in stable housing when facing eviction, loss of utilities, foreclosure, and other housing emergencies. It provides qualifying households up to $7,000 in a 12-month period to preserve current housing or move to new housing, and can cover overdue utilities, moving costs, and overdue rent or mortgage payments. Way Finders helps tenants and homeowners with the online application at its Housing Centers or by phone.
program.contact: Way Finders: 413-233-1500, info@wayfinders.org; Northampton Housing Center, 256 Pleasant Street, Northampton, MA 01060

requirements.text: For households facing eviction, loss of utilities, foreclosure, or other housing emergencies. Up to $7,000 per household in a 12-month period.
For households facing eviction, loss of utilities, foreclosure, or other housing emergencies. Up to $7,000 per household in a 12-month period.
RAFT requires an application from both the tenant or homeowner and the landlord. For other emergency needs such as overdue utilities or moving costs, only the household must apply.
The Commonwealth requires renter, homeowner, and landlord applications and documents to be uploaded directly into its online system. Way Finders can help if you need assistance applying.
